correctness.rationale: On fixed mass the incoming-minus-outgoing flux relative to the proposed product weight is h(c)−h(b) for a rightward directed pair; checking the nine pairs gives h=(0,1+t,(1+t)²), hence telescoping around the ring, and reversal gives the same balance for left hops. Right-hop rates are positive on every allowed right transfer; the underlying undirected transfer graph is connected at fixed mass and the positive stationary law rules out transient classes, giving uniqueness also at q=0. The fixed-mass fugacity gauge gives the symmetric three-point law conditioned on sum d=N−L. Requiring one or two zero increments gives the exact probability ratios and determinant. At d=0, the nonnegative, nonconstant characteristic function supplies strict Cauchy–Schwarz for consecutive moments, giving positive pair covariance and increasing conditional probabilities; fixed sum and exchangeability give the opposite sign for ordinary occupations. This is pairwise covariance and conditional singleton monotonicity, not a full multivariate association claim. For d/√L→c, symmetrizing the determinant before expansion retains the exact squared characteristic-function difference. To justify domination explicitly, φ(θ)≤exp(−4pθ²/π²) on [−π,π], and after scaling L times the difference is bounded by p(u²+v²). The tilted Gaussian second-square variance is 1/(2p²)−c²/(2p³), giving L² times the covariance equal in the limit to a²(1−c²/p)/2. The ordinary variance tends to 2p. Uniform slot counting at t=1 gives the two hypergeometric singleton probabilities, whose difference factors as stated; the extreme masses have deterministic indicators. Numerical coefficient propagation independently checked both signs (e.g. at w=2.5 and L=2000, scaled covariances are 0.154524 at d=0 and −0.247380 at d=34, compared with leading terms 0.154321 and −0.247068). Uploaded check.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. No sign is determined on the limiting boundary, nor an all-density finite threshold for general t.
